episodes.192475: Scattered to numerous thunderstorms developed along a stationary frontal boundary oriented in a north/south manner through eastern Alabama through much of the day. This produced isolated strong thunderstorms that produced some damaging wind gusts that knocked down a few trees.
episodes.192481: The monsoon high slid east of NM over TX bringing monsoon moisture northward into NM. Slow steering flow coupled with moisture allowed for two more days of burn scar flash flooding on the complex of burn scars in and around Ruidoso. The first of which caused only a minor road closure near Mechem Drive. The second of which was far more widespread bringing impacts from Alto to Ruidoso to Ruidoso Downs.
episodes.192575: A deep moisture profile and an increase of deep-layer shear over Central Alabama on July 28 resulted in very efficient rainfall occurring over central and northern parts of the region. Precipitable water values of 2.1 to 2.2 inches aided high instantaneous rain rates, at times on the order of 5-7 in/hr. Sporadic flooding occurred in Marion County during the early afternoon as two rounds of heavy rainfall moved through the area. By late afternoon, training thunderstorms over the Cahaba Heights area quickly flooded area homes and streets before another, much larger, round of thunderstorms overtook Jefferson County from the west. Many of the southern and western suburbs of Birmingham experienced flooding of homes and roadways during the early evening hours as 3-5 inches of rain fell across these areas.||The next day, an MCS tracking into northeast Alabama from Tennessee resulted in several trees being blown down in Cherokee County, especially the Centre and Cedar Bluff areas.
episodes.192704: Summertime thunderstorms impacted Middle Tennessee on July 28, 2024. One of these typical summertime storms produced heavy rain in Macon County, causing flooding in the Lafayette area.
episodes.192925: A severe thunderstorm impacted the Willcox area resulting in 1 inch hail and downed power poles due to strong winds.
episodes.192990: Slow moving thunderstorms produced localized flash flooding across the area.
episodes.193131: Sufficient moisture in combination with a shortwave impulse brushing by the area resulted in numerous strong thunderstorm wind gusts in addition to isolated instances of flash flooding.
episodes.193185: Showers and thunderstorms with gusty winds moved across portions of southeast Wyoming on the afternoon of the 28th with wind gusts around 65 mph reported along Interstate 80 near Elk Mountain.
episodes.193217: Storms developed over the Nebraska panhandle during the afternoon with hail and strong winds eventually forming into a convective line that propagated into central Nebraska. Additional storms with strong winds moved east out of Wyoming into western Nebraska bringing another round of strong winds into the evening.
episodes.193218: Storms with gusty winds developed early in the afternoon across southeast to south-central Wyoming before organizing into a convective line moving west to east across the area. Strong winds up to 70 mph were reported with these storms.
episodes.193776: A broken line of thunderstorms developed over the northeastern Nebraska Panhandle during the late afternoon hours of July 27th. As this activity moved to the southeast, it produced wind gusts to 60 MPH in western Cherry and Lincoln counties.
episodes.193839: Strong to severe thunderstorms tracked along the Colorado/Nebraska border dropping hail up to 2 inches in diameter and producing winds to 66 mph.
episodes.193968: In the late afternoon of the 28th, a few storms began to fire. One storm, northwest of St. Francis, grew rapidly and stayed strong over the next several hours as it moved southeast. It produced baseball sized hail and estimated winds of 80 MPH which caused property damage.
episodes.193971: In the afternoon of the 27th, a line of storms formed in the panhandle of Nebraska and proceeded southeast over the next several hours. These storms went on to produce wind gusts up 64 MPH in Hitchcock County.
episodes.194054: The remains of an MCV that tracked across Nebraska earlier in the day moved into Iowa in the late afternoon. These remnants moved into a deeply unstable environment with 2000+ J/kg of SBCAPE and intensified through the early evening, transitioning to a loosely organized bowing segment in the evening. Steep mid and low level lapse rates and DCAPE of 750-1000 J/kg were also available. This combination resulted in a handful of hail and damaging wind gusts across the area.  Heavy rain also occurred as a line of training convection developed behind the bowing segment lasting late into the night. A swath of 3 to 5 inches of rain occurred with the system in central to southern Iowa, however no flood impacts were noted.
episodes.194140: A thunderstorm briefly became severe over eastern Fall River County into southwestern Oglala Lakota County, producing wind gusts to around 60 mph.
episodes.194141: A severe thunderstorm tracked across far southern Oglala Lakota County, producing wind gusts to 60 mph in the Pine Ridge area.
episodes.194145: A severe thunderstorm developed over southeast Crook County and moved into South Dakota, producing hail to quarter size in the Beulah area.
episodes.194146: A line of severe thunderstorms with strong wind gusts developed across central and southern portions of Campbell County and tracked east into southern Crook and Weston counties.
episodes.194148: A thunderstorm became severe over the eastern slopes of the central Black Hills and tracked east-southeast onto the adjacent plains before weakening over eastern Custer County. The storm produced hail to golf ball size from near Rockerville to Hermosa.
episodes.194151: A severe thunderstorm tracked east-southeast out of northeast Wyoming and across the northern Black Hills. The storm produced large hail and wind gusts to over 60 mph.
episodes.194293: A negatively titled mid-level trough moved through the Mid-South on July 28, 2024. The trough interacted with a moist and unstable airmass in place across the Mid-South to produce scattered thunderstorms across north Mississippi with isolated wind damage.
episodes.194395: Training heavy rainfall developed in portions of Southern Illinois during the evening hours on the 28th, with flash flooding developing in Wayne and Saline Counties. Eldorado was hit hard for a second time with rainfall totals around 5 inches, prompting water rescues. Water intruded into buildings including the Ferrell Hospital, which had already been heavily impacted from a flood in May. PW values were up to 2 inches.
episodes.194469: An upper trough was approaching the Rockies and a few storms developed ahead of it in Hidalgo county where modest moisture remained in place.
episodes.194689: Thunderstorms developed along a surface boundary in an environment of elevated instability and marginal deep layer shear. Some of the storms became severe over Grant, Morton, and Burleigh Counties producing large hail and severe wind gusts. The largest hail, which was the size of a half-dollar, occurred on the west end of Mandan in Morton County. The strongest reported wind gusts, estimated at 70 mph, occurred to the north of Lark in Grant County, and on the west end of Mandan in Morton County.
episodes.194835: Scattered thunderstorms developed along a stationary surface boundary which was across northern MN to eastern SD. Most of the thunderstorms were sub-severe, however a few did produce periods of heavy rainfall and strong wind gusts. A few trees were downed in Yellow Medicine and Wright Counties.
episodes.194953: Localized heavy rainfall fell across the area and produced some flash flooding.
episodes.195015: Scattered, slow-moving convection beneath a humid high pressure ridge produced isolated flash flooding.
episodes.195054: Storms developed along a weak surface boundary within a moisture-rich environment with weak mean-layer flow. Slow moving storms produced rainfall rates of 3 to 4 inches per hour, with amounts of 3.09 inches reported by a cooperative weather observer near Wakefield and personal automated gauges and radar estimates up to 4 inches over portions of the Sioux City metro area.
episodes.195069: Storms developed along a weak surface boundary within a moisture-rich environment with weak mean-layer flow. Slow moving storms produced rainfall rates of 3 to 4 inches per hour, with amounts of 3.09 inches reported by a cooperative weather observer near Wakefield and personal automated gauges and radar estimates up to 4 inches over portions of the Sioux City metro area.
episodes.195190: Deep monsoon moisture triggered strong to severe thunderstorms with hail and heavy rain over parts of northern Arizona.
episodes.195272: A shortwave passing through the region resulted in scattered thunderstorms through the day, some of which produced severe wind gusts.

Numerous reports of flooded roadways, homes, and businesses were received across parts of southern and western Jefferson County, including Cahaba Heights, Vestavia Hills, Homewood, Hoover, Midfield, Hueytown, and McCalla. Several roads were temporarily impassable, including Interstate 459 at Interstate 59/20 in McCalla and U.S. Highway 31 in Homewood.
